hook.en: In a class, 20 students play cricket and 15 play football. Are 35 students playing a sport? Not if some play both. The *addition theorem* fixes this double count.
hook.kn: ಒಂದು ತರಗತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ 20 ವಿದ್ಯಾರ್ಥಿಗಳು ಕ್ರಿಕೆಟ್, 15 ಫುಟ್‌ಬಾಲ್ ಆಡುತ್ತಾರೆ. 35 ಜನ ಆಟವಾಡುತ್ತಾರೆಯೆ? ಕೆಲವರು ಎರಡನ್ನೂ ಆಡಿದರೆ ಇಲ್ಲ. ಸಂಕಲನ ಪ್ರಮೇಯ ಈ ಎರಡು ಬಾರಿ ಎಣಿಕೆಯನ್ನು ಸರಿಪಡಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: State and use the addition theorem

say.en: In a class, 20 students play cricket and 15 play football. Are 35 students playing a sport? Not if some play both. The addition theorem fixes this double count. In this lesson: State and use the addition theorem.
Use P(A′) equals 1 - PA.

body.en: For any two events, $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A \cap B)$. The overlap is subtracted because it was counted in both P(A) and P(B). For mutually exclusive events $P(A \cap B) = 0$ and $P(A \cup B) = P(A) + P(B)$. Also $P(A') = 1 - P(A)$. For three events, $P(A \cup B \cup C) = \sum P(A) - \sum P(A \cap B) + P(A \cap B \cap C)$.
body.kn: ಯಾವುದೇ ಎರಡು ಘಟನೆಗಳಿಗೆ P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B). ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಭಾಗ ಎರಡು ಬಾರಿ ಎಣಿಕೆಯಾಗಿರುವುದರಿಂದ ಒಮ್ಮೆ ಕಳೆಯುತ್ತೇವೆ. ಪರಸ್ಪರ ವರ್ಜಿತ ಘಟನೆಗಳಿಗೆ P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B). P(A′) = 1 − P(A).

say.en: For any two events, P(A \cup B) equals PA plus PB - P(A \cap B). The overlap is subtracted because it was counted in both PA and PB. For mutually exclusive events P(A \cap B) equals 0 and P(A \cup B) equals PA plus PB. Also P(A') equals 1 - PA. For three events, P(A \cup B \cup C) = \sum PA - \sum P(A \cap B) plus P(A \cap B \cap C). "or" means union.
say.kn: ಯಾವುದೇ ಎರಡು ಘಟನೆಗಳಿಗೆ PA union B equals PA plus PB - PA intersection B. ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಭಾಗ ಎರಡು ಬಾರಿ ಎಣಿಕೆಯಾಗಿರುವುದರಿಂದ ಒಮ್ಮೆ ಕಳೆಯುತ್ತೇವೆ. ಪರಸ್ಪರ ವರ್ಜಿತ ಘಟನೆಗಳಿಗೆ PA union B equals PA plus PB. P(A′) equals 1 - PA.

say.en: Subtract the overlap once.
P(A′) equals 1 - PA.

problem.en: P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4, P(A ∩ B) = 0.2. Find P(A ∪ B) and P(neither A nor B).

narration.en: Let us work this out together. P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4, P(A ∩ B) = 0.2. Find P(A ∪ B) and P(neither A nor B).

say.en: Let us work this out together. PA equals 0.5, PB equals 0.4, PA intersection B equals 0.2. Find PA union B and Pneither A nor B.
PA union B equals 0.5 plus 0.4 minus 0.2 equals 0.7.
Pneither equals 1 - PA union B equals 1 minus 0.7 equals 0.3.
So the answer is 0.7 and 0.3.

problem.en: A number is chosen from 1 to 30. Find the probability that it is a multiple of 3 or of 5.

steps.en: Multiples of 3: 10. Multiples of 5: 6. Multiples of 15: 2.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A number is chosen from 1 to 30. Find the probability that it is a multiple of 3 or of 5.

say.en: Let us work this out together. A number is chosen from 1 to 30. Find the probability that it is a multiple of 3 or of 5.
Multiples of 3: 10. Multiples of 5: 6. Multiples of 15: 2.
P equals 10 over 30 plus 6 over 30 minus 2 over 30 equals 14 over 30.
= 7 over 15.
So the answer is 7 over 15.

body.en: In probability "or" means union, so you add; "and" means intersection, the overlap. Every time you add two events that can happen together, remove the overlap once.
